narrativeReportMd:
# MolecularSequence R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`MolecularSequence` appears to have been removed from the R6 core ballot package rather than renamed in-place. This is a hard R4-to-R6 breaking change: an R4 instance with `resourceType: "MolecularSequence"` has no R6 core StructureDefinition or resource type to validate against.

## Scope
The analysis used the supplied R4 MolecularSequence StructureDefinition, both package indexes, package metadata, MolecularSequence-specific R4 terminology artifacts, and targeted searches of the R6 core package for likely successors. Inherited base-resource changes were excluded. R4 search parameters and non-core implementation guide mappings were not independently assessed.

## Main migration themes
The main issue is not a local cardinality or type tweak; it is resource removal. R4 systems must replace the entire MolecularSequence model, including required `coordinateSystem`, reference sequence, variant, quality, repository, self-pointer, and structural-variant content. R6 core does not provide a computable same-artifact target or a ConceptMap, so migration is likely profile- or implementation-specific and potentially lossy.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is the absent R6 resource definition (`MolecularSequence:ARTIFACT_IDENTITY:root:2f1c8e`). Generated R6 models and resource registries will not contain a `MolecularSequence` class/resource type, and the MolecularSequence-specific R4 terminology artifacts are also absent from the R6 core package.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most needed for conversion design. The local package evidence does not prove whether the intended replacement is Observation-based genomics profiling, DiagnosticReport/DocumentReference attachments, external repositories, or an implementation-guide-defined model.

## Backward-compatible design observations
A less disruptive design would have been to retain a deprecated or trial-use `MolecularSequence` StructureDefinition in R6 while introducing successor patterns and mappings. The supplied inputs do not include the ballot rationale, so this report cannot assess whether removal was justified by Clinical Genomics redesign decisions.

## Follow-up analysis
Follow-up should examine MolecularSequence search parameters, any official R4/R5/R6 cross-version mappings, Clinical Genomics implementation guides, and terminology package movement for the removed sequence-oriented code systems and value sets.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `MolecularSequence` is present in R4 but absent from the R6 core package, with no clear renamed/split core successor found. The top migration concerns are resource-type validation failure, loss of the complete local sequence content model, and missing MolecularSequence-specific terminology/codegen surfaces. The main uncertainty is the intended official replacement pattern, which would require narrative ballot notes or a ConceptMap.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is an artifact-level redesign rather than an element-level patch. R4 data using `coordinateSystem`, `referenceSeq`, `variant`, `observedSeq`, `quality`, `repository`, `pointer`, and `structureVariant` cannot be made R6-core-conformant by renaming a few paths. Implementers will likely need a domain-specific mapping to Observation/DiagnosticReport/DocumentReference/profiles/extensions or retention of R4 MolecularSequence in a compatibility layer.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the R6 core package lacks a `MolecularSequence` StructureDefinition and related core resource type evidence, because the supplied path is absent and targeted package/index searches found no same-name or sequence/genomics resource successor. Confidence is medium on the intended migration target because official narrative diffs, ballot rationale, and cross-version ConceptMaps were not supplied.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The match attempt started with the exact canonical/resource name and then searched R6 filenames, index entries, and StructureDefinition content for molecular, sequence, genomic, genetic, variant, chromosome, and allele terms. No R6 core resource successor was found.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation break. A conformant R4 instance with `resourceType: "MolecularSequence"` cannot be validated as an R6 core resource because the R6 package has no resource definition with that type. Runtime risk is critical for parsers, validators, REST endpoints, subscriptions, search APIs, and generated code that expect the resource registry to include MolecularSequence.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The resource carries genomic sequence, variant, and repository details. Systems that exchange genetic testing data could lose clinically relevant sequence/variant context unless an explicit migration model is selected.

justification.inferredGoal: Likely replacement or retirement of an early Trial Use Clinical Genomics resource model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep a deprecated core R6 `MolecularSequence` resource as a transitional compatibility bridge while steering new genomics content to successor patterns.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of retiring or replacing an early Trial Use/FMM 1 genomics resource is reasonable, and the R6 package evidence shows no same-resource successor. Because `MolecularSequence` was low maturity, R6 had more latitude to make a disruptive cleanup than it would for mature normative content. The break is still severe, and the local inputs do not prove the official ballot rationale, so this is only probably justified rather than fully justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have retained `MolecularSequence` in R6 as a deprecated or retired resource for at least a transition release, with guidance to use the redesigned genomics representation for new content. That would preserve validation, parsers, generated classes, endpoints, and most existing R4 instances. It is only a partial alternative because it would keep the old same-resource model in the core package, create parallel ways to represent genomic sequence facts, and risk the deprecated resource never disappearing. Conversion tooling, external profiles, or an R6-to-R4 backport extension can help migration, but they are mitigations rather than a backward-compatible base R6 design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances and generated surfaces, but leaves an immature retired resource in core and risks duplicate genomics representations persisting indefinitely.

findings.narrativeMd: `MolecularSequence` was a concrete R4 resource and is not present in the R6 core package. This is the strongest breaking pattern for instances: validators fail before reaching individual elements because the resource type itself is not recognized. Implementers cannot fix this by changing cardinalities or choice suffixes; they need a replacement representation or an R4 compatibility island.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid is direct: any R4 resource instance with `resourceType = MolecularSequence` is outside the R6 core resource set found in the supplied package. Strict parsers may reject it as an unknown resource type, generated R6 model libraries may have no class, and REST servers may have no endpoint or search compartment for it. R6-to-R4 representability is marked not applicable because no R6 MolecularSequence artifact exists to reverse-map.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all stored and exchanged R4 MolecularSequence resources. Decide whether to preserve them in R4 form, map them to an implementation-guide-defined R6 genomics profile, attach sequence data as documents/repository links, or represent clinical interpretations as Observations/DiagnosticReports. Test validators and resource registries explicitly for unknown-resource handling and ensure downstream systems do not silently drop genomic content.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The removal may reflect a legitimate redesign of an immature Trial Use resource, but retaining a deprecated R6 resource or publishing a formal ConceptMap would have reduced breakage. Without an official migration artifact, the compatibility burden shifts to implementers.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 defines `MolecularSequence` as a concrete resource, while the assigned R6 package has no same resource definition or exact index entry. That is a top-level R4-to-R6 break: an existing instance cannot be treated as a base R6 resource, and clients relying on resource-type dispatch have no core R6 target. FMM 1 makes removal of an immature trial-use resource more acceptable than it would be for mature content, but this is not merely speculative churn: HL7 genomics guidance and the HLA reporting IG show MolecularSequence as part of clinical genomics reporting patterns. Because a deprecated or retired R6 StructureDefinition could have preserved historical validation and dispatch while warning against new use, the complete resource identity removal deserves renewed standards/design review.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition-MolecularSequence.json: url http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/MolecularSequence, kind resource, type MolecularSequence, abstract false, FMM 1, trial-use.
R6 package: StructureDefinition-MolecularSequence.json is absent and exact MolecularSequence search in .index.json returned no entry.
R6 package genomics search found no obvious core successor resource; only familymemberhistory-genetic appeared as a genomics-like StructureDefinition.
HL7 Genomics Reporting IG Appendix G says MolecularSequence can hold clinically relevant sequence data and be used with IG profiles; it also notes overlap/redundancy under evaluation.
HLA Reporting IG says it constrains MolecularSequence to report sequencing results together with novel variants.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1/trial-use substantially softens the baseline stability expectation, so I did not infer broad production impact from removal alone. The clinical genomics/HLA IG evidence and safety-sensitive domain keep the concern material despite low maturity.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen: an R4 resourceType MolecularSequence has no base R6 StructureDefinition, so validation, parser dispatch, conformance, and any resource-type keyed APIs lose the core target.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base R6 design exists: keep MolecularSequence as deprecated or retired for a transition release, ideally with migration guidance to the intended genomics reporting pattern. The tradeoff is real because it leaves an immature and possibly redundant model in core and may prolong parallel representations, but it would preserve historical instance validity and resource identity at modest technical cost.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Critical impact and Partial alternative judgment; the mechanism is real, but the fresh review gives more weight to FMM 1 and uses specific IG evidence rather than assuming broad prevalence.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: This is not a path rename match. The finding groups the R4 local content model because no R6 MolecularSequence artifact exists and no likely core resource successor was found.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The hard validation break is already captured by the resource-removal finding. This finding captures the migration/conversion break: even if an implementation chooses an R6 alternative such as Observation, DiagnosticReport, DocumentReference, extensions, or an external repository, the R4 local model is rich enough that a lossless generic transform is unlikely without domain rules.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Lossy conversion can obscure coordinate-system conventions, reference sequence identity, observed/reference allele details, quality metrics, repository access method, and structural variant boundaries.

justification.inferredGoal: Move genomic sequence representation out of this early resource model or replace it with profile-based clinical genomics patterns.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 local content model in a deprecated R6 `MolecularSequence` resource, or carry key sequence details in optional base successor elements if a core successor existed.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving away from the R4 local model may be reasonable if Clinical Genomics intentionally replaced it with better Observation, DiagnosticReport, DocumentReference, repository, or implementation-guide patterns. The supplied core package does not show that rationale or a computable successor mapping, so the reasonableness of losing the 69 local element definitions and invariants cannot be judged confidently.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have preserved the R4 content model in a deprecated R6 `MolecularSequence` resource, or, if R6 introduced a core successor, included optional elements/backbones for the key R4 sequence, reference, variant, quality, repository, pointer, and structural-variant facts. That would preserve more R4-valid content than ordinary migration guidance. It remains only a partial alternative because it would carry substantial immature detail into R6, create validation and implementation burden, and might leave duplicate representations for the same genomic facts indefinitely. A ConceptMap or StructureMap would be valuable but, by itself, is conversion tooling rather than a backward-compatible base design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would reduce data loss for common R4 content, but preserves a broad low-maturity model and could duplicate or conflict with the intended R6 genomics design.

examples.examplesMd: The Observation example is not asserted to be an official R6 mapping. It demonstrates that a naive migration target needs extra profile guidance or extensions to preserve MolecularSequence-specific semantics.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 MolecularSequence is not just a wrapper around one observation; it contains a specialized model for biological sequence raw data, variants, sequence quality, repositories, and structural variants. R6 core provides no matching target in the supplied package. That makes conversion a modeling exercise, not a mechanical path migration.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: The resource-removal finding causes old-valid/new-invalid validation failure. At the model level, the risk is loss of semantic validation: constraints such as `msq-3`, `msq-5`, and `msq-6` no longer travel with the data unless the chosen R6 target recreates them. Strict FHIRPath, ETL, analytics, and clinical decision support rules that referenced these R4 paths will fail or become semantically incomplete.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not bulk-convert MolecularSequence resources into generic Observations without preserving coordinate convention, reference sequence identity, allele strings, quality metrics, repository access details, and structural variant intervals. Define a project-specific mapping, preferably backed by profiles/extensions and test cases for 0-based versus 1-based coordinates, referenceSeq alternatives, self-pointers, and structural variant boundaries.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A formal compatibility profile or ConceptMap could have reduced ambiguity while still allowing the R6 model to move forward. Without such an artifact, implementers must infer the mapping from local business context, which increases interoperability risk.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review should confirm whether the current R6 ballot intentionally moved sequence details to a separate implementation guide or external terminology/model package not present in the supplied core package.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The R4 local model is not just a shell around common DomainResource fields; it contains required coordinate-system data, reference-sequence alternatives, variant alleles and coordinates, quality metrics, repository pointers, and structural-variant details. With no computable R6 core successor in the local package, migration into Observation, DiagnosticReport, DocumentReference, extensions, or an external genomics repository would require domain-specific choices. That makes this a lossy or expert-mediated migration risk for sequence facts used downstream by clinical genomics reports, even though the source resource is low maturity.

R4 MolecularSequence.coordinateSystem is required and constrained by msq-3 to values 0 or 1.
R4 referenceSeq has msq-5 and msq-6 governing genomeBuild/chromosome pairing and exactly one reference-sequence representation.
R4 element extraction showed local variant, observedSeq, quality, repository, pointer, and structureVariant content.
R6 package/index searches found no MolecularSequence or obvious core sequence/genomics successor StructureDefinition.
HL7 Genomics Reporting conversion guidance says older genomics profiles are superseded by the IG and that MolecularSequence/Observation boundaries were still under evaluation.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1/trial-use softens the expectation that every local detail remain stable. It does not eliminate the concern because the affected details include coordinate conventions and allele/quality/repository facts whose migration can require clinical genomics judgment.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid with migration loss: no base R6 core model accepts the R4 local MolecularSequence backbone, and transforms to other resources or extensions may lose or reinterpret sequence coordinates, alleles, quality, or repository semantics.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design would either retain the deprecated R4 local model or provide a named R6 successor/profile with computable mappings for the key sequence, variant, quality, and repository fields. Retaining the entire model has significant cost because it preserves a broad low-maturity design and may conflict with the Observation-centered genomics direction, but providing no computable bridge leaves too much expert-dependent migration.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment; I agree the migration risk is substantive, while tempering prevalence because the source artifact is FMM 1.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The terminology artifacts were matched by the exact R4 ValueSet/CodeSystem ids used by MolecularSequence bindings. The R6 core package index returned no exact entries for those ids.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The whole resource is already invalid in R6, but the terminology removal is a separate migration/codegen risk. justification.inferredGoal: Retire terminology dedicated to a removed Trial Use resource.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Retiring terminology dedicated to a removed Trial Use resource is understandable, but the same cleanup goal could likely have been met while preserving deprecated CodeSystems and ValueSets for historical data. Unlike retaining the whole resource, retaining retired terminology has a smaller core-model cost and does not require supporting a live R6 `MolecularSequence` endpoint. On the available evidence, removing the terminology surface appears more avoidable than the resource removal itself.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest backward-compatible base design is to keep the R4 sequence type, orientation, strand, quality, repository, chromosome, and sequence-reference ValueSets/CodeSystems in the R6 package with deprecated or retired status and clear notes that no current core R6 resource binds to them. That would let validators and generators continue resolving historical codings while still discouraging new use. ConceptMaps to successor vocabularies would be helpful, but they are complementary migration aids; the base-design alternative is retaining resolvable deprecated terminology.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Low to moderate tradeoff: dormant terminology remains visible, but it avoids breaking historical code validation and enum generation.

examples.examplesMd: The example highlights codes from R4 MolecularSequence-specific required bindings. In R6 core there is no MolecularSequence resource or same-id terminology surface for these bindings.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 MolecularSequence carried several small domain-specific code systems and value sets. Their absence from R6 core means migration cannot simply keep the same bound element paths and expect R6 validators or generated enums to know these codes.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: As pure R6 resources, old MolecularSequence instances are invalid because the resource is gone. If an implementer preserves these fields in R6 extensions or profiles, terminology validation is still a risk: same-id R6 core ValueSets were not found, so validators may need the R4 terminology package or explicit successor terminology.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Preserve the original coding system URIs and versions when carrying historical MolecularSequence data forward. findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping retired terminology would have been a relatively low-cost compatibility bridge even if the resource was removed. The tradeoff is that dormant code systems remain visible in the core package and may imply more support for legacy sequence modeling than R6 intends.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The R4 MolecularSequence-specific code systems and value sets are not present in the R6 core package, but this is not a meaningful separate R6 base-model break once the resource and its bound elements have been removed. Historical R4 validation can still be performed against the R4 package, and a R6-only package has no current base element that needs these bindings. Implementers migrating old sequence data may need to load R4 terminology or map codes, but that is secondary to the resource/model migration rather than an independent reason to revisit R6 core terminology packaging.

findings.title: R6 generated models, parsers, and REST/search APIs will not expose MolecularSequence

oldState.summary: R4 package index includes the MolecularSequence StructureDefinition and multiple MolecularSequence search parameters.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 code generators and servers commonly derive a resource class, parser dispatch entry, REST endpoint, compartment/search metadata, and strongly typed search constants from the core package.

newState.summary: R6 core package index contains no MolecularSequence StructureDefinition or MolecularSequence search parameters.
newState.narrativeMd: A generator built only from the R6 core package will not produce a `MolecularSequence` resource class or same-resource search API.

facts.field: search parameters observed in package index

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The finding follows from exact package-index presence in R4 and absence in R6 for the assigned resource identity.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is primarily a software break rather than an additional instance-validation rule. Source code importing `MolecularSequence`, switch statements over resource types, database tables keyed by resource type, REST routes, search parameter constants, serializers, and FHIRPath expressions over MolecularSequence paths can fail to compile or return unknown-resource errors after regenerating against R6.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Operational systems may stop accepting or returning genomic sequence data, causing workflow gaps even where the data remains stored historically.

justification.inferredGoal: Remove obsolete generated surfaces for a removed resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated R6 resource and search-parameter definitions so generated models, parsers, and REST/search metadata can continue exposing MolecularSequence.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: If retiring the low-maturity `MolecularSequence` resource is accepted as the R6 base goal, then removing the generated model, parser, registry, endpoint, and search surfaces follows from that goal. The runtime break is large, but keeping those surfaces would materially blur whether `MolecularSequence` is still an R6 core resource. Because the official rationale is not in the local inputs, this is probably rather than conclusively justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design would have retained deprecated `MolecularSequence` StructureDefinition and SearchParameter entries so code generators could continue producing resource classes, parser dispatch, REST routes, and search constants while warning implementers away from new use. This is a partial alternative because it preserves old APIs and may encourage continued production use of a retired model. Separate library adapters or compatibility modules are useful mitigations, but unless the core R6 package retains the resource/search definitions, they are not themselves backward-compatible base-design alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Eases upgrades for existing systems, but keeps obsolete generated APIs and endpoints in the R6 conformance surface.

evidence.detail: R4 package index includes the MolecularSequence StructureDefinition.
R4 package index includes multiple MolecularSequence search parameters, including identifier, patient, type, chromosome, variant coordinate, and window coordinate parameters.
R6 package index search found no MolecularSequence StructureDefinition, instances, or MolecularSequence search parameters.

examples.examplesMd: A typical break is generated-code failure such as an import of `MolecularSequence`, an enum case for `ResourceType.MolecularSequence`, or a REST route `/MolecularSequence` disappearing after regenerating from R6 definitions.

findings.narrativeMd: The resource removal affects more than validation. Many FHIR stacks generate resource classes, parser dispatch tables, REST route metadata, and search constants directly from core StructureDefinitions and SearchParameters. Those generated surfaces disappear when the R6 package lacks MolecularSequence.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: The instance-level validator will reject the resource type, while runtime systems may fail earlier at deserialization or routing. FHIRPath expressions and query builders referencing `MolecularSequence.referenceSeq.windowStart`, `variant.start`, or search parameters such as `chromosome` will not have R6 definitions to bind to.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Before upgrading generated libraries, search code for `MolecularSequence`, `/MolecularSequence`, and MolecularSequence search parameter names. Add an explicit compatibility module for historical R4 data, or migrate data and APIs to selected R6 profiles. Include negative tests for unknown-resource rejection and positive tests for whatever compatibility path is chosen.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The least disruptive runtime approach would be a separate legacy adapter rather than pretending MolecularSequence remains R6-conformant. That keeps R6 clean while making breakage explicit and testable.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This finding is the software-surface consequence of the resource removal, and it is independently important because generated R6 artifacts will not expose a MolecularSequence class, resource registry entry, REST endpoint, or MolecularSequence search constants. An implementation that used the R4 Genomics Reporting or HLA reporting patterns could fail at compile time or route/conformance time even before instance validation is considered. Low FMM means the standard was allowed to evolve, but for a clinically relevant genomics resource a transition surface would have reduced upgrade shock.
keyEvidence: R4 package index includes StructureDefinition-MolecularSequence.json.
R4 package index includes 13 SearchParameter-MolecularSequence-* files, including identifier, patient, type, chromosome, variant coordinate, and window coordinate searches.
R6 package index exact checks found no MolecularSequence StructureDefinition and no SearchParameter-MolecularSequence-* entries.
HL7 Genomics Reporting IG and HLA Reporting IG document MolecularSequence use in clinical genomics reporting patterns.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1/trial-use lowers the expectation that generated APIs must be preserved forever. The clinical genomics implementation evidence and the breadth of the removed resource/search surface keep this from being dismissed as harmless churn.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: R6 generation from the core package omits MolecularSequence models, parser registry cases, REST/search metadata, and search-parameter constants that R4 implementations could have compiled or configured against.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design would retain deprecated MolecularSequence and its search parameters in R6 conformance resources while marking them non-preferred for new use. This has the same tradeoff as the resource alternative: it preserves old APIs and endpoints but may encourage ongoing dependence on a retired low-maturity model and duplicate genomics representations.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High runtime impact and Partial alternative judgment; I agree the generated/API break is substantial, while tempering expected prevalence because the resource was FMM 1.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 still contains a Clinical Genomics profile, but it is not a MolecularSequence successor
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `familymemberhistory-genetic` constrains `FamilyMemberHistory`; it does not define or replace the `MolecularSequence` resource type. It is therefore not itself a breaking change to MolecularSequence.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Its presence shows Clinical Genomics content is not entirely absent from R6 core, but it should not be used as evidence of a MolecularSequence migration path without additional official guidance.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R4 MolecularSequence was Trial Use/FMM 1
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The maturity/status metadata does not itself change any instance. It helps explain why later FHIR ballots may have redesigned or removed the artifact.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Despite lower maturity, production systems that adopted the R4 resource still face hard validation and runtime breaks when moving to R6 core.
